rulings.summary: Starting hands are five cards; the Corp may mulligan before the Runner, and a mulliganed player keeps the second hand.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet setup order and mulligan prompts are Corp first, then Runner; no third hand is offered.

rulings.summary: Clicks are the basic unit of activity; the Corp receives three and the Runner receives four each turn.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet turn traces allot three Corp clicks and four Runner clicks before their action phases.

rulings.summary: A player wins at the next checkpoint when their score reaches seven agenda points.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet checks the seven-point threshold at checkpoints, including after score and steal effects.

rulings.summary: Advancing is the Corp basic action that spends one click and one credit; only advanceable cards may be advanced.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet offers advance only for legal installed cards and records the counter before checkpoint effects.

rulings.summary: Placed or loaded objects are hosted, hosted is distinct from installed, and host changes/trash follow checkpoint rules.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet preserves host relationships through counters, Trojan installs, and host removal.

rulings.summary: Only one active unique card of a name remains, with the newest active copy surviving at checkpoint.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet enforces uniqueness at checkpoint rather than deck construction.

rulings.summary: A player may have only one active installed console; older active consoles are trashed at checkpoint.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet allows multiple console copies in a deck and resolves the active-most-recent rule in play.

rulings.summary: HQ, R&D, Archives, and the grip have different visibility; facedown Corp cards remain hidden unless a rule requires a reveal.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet observations expose only the viewer's legal hidden-zone choices and revealed cards.

rulings.summary: The Corp turn has draw, action, and discard phases; the Runner turn has action and discard phases.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet emits formal turn-begin/end and phase transitions, including forced action-phase end.

rulings.summary: Basic actions are phase-bound, and the Corp/Runner action sets include gain, draw, install, play, advance, run, tag, and purge costs.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet legality rejects actions outside an action phase and charges the printed click/credit costs.

rulings.summary: The Corp's mandatory draw is not an action; the Runner has no draw phase; drawing from an empty deck is handled by deck-out rules.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet starts the Corp turn with the mandatory draw and reports deck-out before a missing card is silently ignored.

rulings.summary: A player continues actions until no clicks remain unless an ability directly ends the action phase; no voluntary end-turn action is added.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet terminal effects close action windows and continue to discard; leftover clicks are lost at phase end.

rulings.summary: Run position is stable across approach/encounter; an ICE uninstalled mid-encounter is passed and the run continues.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet run traces use ICE identity/position semantics rather than stale list indexes after topology changes.

rulings.summary: A run becomes successful before the breach, and effects tied to successful runs expire with the run unless a card says otherwise.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet applies successful-run triggers before breach and carries run-scoped modifiers through the breach only.

rulings.summary: Access reveals the accessed card to the Runner, permits one mid-access ability, and forces agenda steal after that opportunity.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet exposes access choices only during the access window and ends access when the card moves.

rulings.summary: Draw, install, play, search, score, steal, swap, trash, discard, set-aside, and remove-from-game are explicit card movements or placements.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet replay traces distinguish movements and preserve deterministic order for choices and shuffles.

rulings.summary: Drawing N cards is an ordered procedure with deck-out handling and no hidden-card identity leak to the opponent.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet does not reveal drawn HQ/grip cards to the opponent and applies deck-out at the required step.

rulings.summary: Arranging and shuffling cards preserves the hidden or open status of a zone while applying the instructed order change.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet records explicit arrange/shuffle choices and never exposes the resulting hidden R&D order.

rulings.summary: Installation declares a legal destination, trashes like cards, pays cost, creates servers, changes active state, and then triggers when-installed abilities.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet models the ordered install steps and keeps Corp installed cards facedown/unrezzed until rez.

rulings.summary: Servers have central and remote positions; a remote server is created by installing a root and is removed when it has no cards.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet exposes legal central/remote destinations and removes an empty remote after its last card leaves.

rulings.summary: A breach establishes the access set and resolves each access as a separate ordered instruction.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet applies additional-access modifiers to the breach without exposing cards before their access.

rulings.summary: ICE install cost is one credit per existing ICE protecting the destination; hardware/program/resource use printed cost; Corp root cards have no install cost.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet charges the current ICE count and honors explicit ignore-cost instructions without changing printed costs.

rulings.summary: Hidden cards are not revealed merely to verify ordinary type/server legality; ability-specific requirements can require reveal.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet examples match hidden Brân/Ansel installs: no reveal for ordinary ICE eligibility, reveal only for extra constraints.

rulings.summary: Events and operations are played, paid, made active, resolved, and trashed unless their effect creates an exception or lingering effect.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet keeps run-starting events active through their timing structure and trashes ordinary operations/events afterward.

rulings.summary: Search temporarily permits looking at a hidden zone, then returns/shuffles cards according to the effect without leaking the search contents.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet search effects reveal only explicitly revealed cards and shuffle the searched zone when directed.

rulings.summary: Swapped installed cards exchange locations simultaneously, remain installed, and retain host relationships without reinstall costs.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet swap traces preserve ICE positions and hosted Trojans while updating the active run's stable target.

rulings.summary: Triggered abilities meet conditions even when their source is inactive in the access cases specified by the rules; pending windows are ordered.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet trigger traces distinguish condition occurrence from ability resolution and honor inactive-access exceptions.

rulings.summary: Checkpoints and reaction/interrupt windows resolve state-based legality, unique/console cleanup, memory, server, and win checks.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet and the engine both resolve checkpoint consequences before the next action/priority window.

rulings.summary: Lingering effects have explicit durations and are independent of a source event or operation after creation.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet run/turn duration markers expire at the same occurrence as the corresponding rule duration.

rulings.summary: Virus, advancement, hosted, loaded, and other counters are typed; purge removes virus counters and loaded cards empty at zero.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet keeps hosted counters distinct from player pools and resolves load/empty transitions at checkpoints.

rulings.summary: Load places counters on an object and empty triggers when the specified hosted pool reaches zero.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet resolves load/empty transitions immediately at the required checkpoint and does not mix hosted credits with player credits.

rulings.summary: Illegal memory, host, unique, console, and server states are repaired at checkpoint using an appropriate set chosen by the controlling rules.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet state validation reports and repairs illegal objects at checkpoint instead of allowing an invalid board to persist.

rulings.summary: Tags are persistent state; the Corp trash-resource and Runner remove-tag basic actions have their printed click/credit costs and conditions.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet tag prompts and tag-or-pay choices are legal only for the tagged Runner and preserve tag state through turns.

rulings.summary: Link is an identity/card characteristic and does not alter the basic run cost in Gateway.
rulings.jnetCrossCheck: jnet retains link metadata but charges one click for a basic run for all Gateway identities.
